source: Thientosapol et al., Proc Natl Acad Sci USA 115:4921-4926 (2018), doi:10.1073/pnas.1719771115, 'SAMHD1 enhances immunoglobulin hypermutation by promoting transversion mutation' (Jolly laboratory, Centenary Institute, Sydney). Table 1 'Raw mutation data', transcribed 2026-10-16 from the PMC copy (PMC5948975). Clones: GenBank MH198*-MH200*, 1,795 records, Sanger dideoxy sequencing.
analysis: Not stated beyond the Methods; mutations collated in a 560-bp window, <=47 sorted cells per host.
matrix_orientation: Table 1 is printed as one row per group, with columns 'From G to A,C,T', 'From C to T,G,A', 'From A to G,T,C', 'From T to C,A,G'. Counts below are keyed from>to, as printed.
note: Table 1 counts every sequence independently (total mutations), not unique mutations: each group's total divided by its sequence count reproduces the printed mutations-per-sequence exactly. The deposit names 12 host animals in the wild-type arm where the paper reports 13; the record HOST-AT40 carries 88 clones, about twice every other host and more than the <=47 per host the Methods describe, so two hosts appear to share one name in the deposit. Group totals are otherwise as printed.
claims_tested: Samhd1 inactivation reduced transversions at A:T (P < 0.0001, Fig. 2B i)
Samhd1 inactivation barely changed transitions at A:T (Fig. 2B ii)
Samhd1 inactivation substantially reduced transversions at C:G (P < 0.0001, Fig. 2B iii)
Samhd1 inactivation nearly doubled transitions at C:G (P = 0.0041, Fig. 2B iv)
total Ig mutation was lower in Samhd1 delta/delta but not significantly (P = 0.07, one-way ANOVA)
